__diagram__.text: AI Pair lets a coding agent work in the programmer's editor at a human pace while the programmer watches and can step in. Read left to right: the agent calls tools, a relay passes them to the editor extension, and the extension acts on the editor.

people.text: The two collaborators. The programmer asks for a session; the agent does the work.

agentside.text: The parts that run beside the agent, outside the editor.

extension.text: Everything that runs inside VS Code: it receives the agent's requests, plays them out, and reports back.

programmer.text: The person who asks the agent to pair and watches the work in VS Code. They can reply, pause, or interrupt at any time.

agent.text: The AI coding agent. It cannot touch the editor directly; it only calls a small set of pairing tools.

relay.text: A small program the agent starts. It offers the pairing tools, finds the right VS Code window, and forwards each call there.

protocol.text: The shared definition of every message the relay and the extension exchange. Both sides check messages against it, so neither misreads the other.

bridge.text: The extension's front door. It accepts only the relay that holds the right secret, then passes each tool call to the session.

controller.text: The session's brain. It lines up the agent's work, decides what to refuse, and writes the report the agent reads next.

player.text: Carries out queued work the way a person would: typing character by character, moving the cursor, pausing to read.

vscode.text: The part that actually changes VS Code: edits text, moves the cursor, runs terminal commands, and shows the narration panel.

__diagram__.text: The same system as the overview, split into its working parts. Start with the relay, follow a call across the wire to the session, then to the editor.

agent.text: Runs next to the agent and turns its tool calls into messages for the editor.

wire.text: The agreed message format that both ends of the connection use.

session.text: The editor-independent core: it holds the session's state and plays work out.

ide.text: The VS Code-specific code: the editor adapter, the narration panel, and start-up wiring.

relay.text: The tool server the agent talks to. It checks each call, forwards it to the editor, and turns the editor's answer into text the agent can read. It keeps no session state.

link.text: The relay's connection to the editor. It looks for a running VS Code window that has the agent's project open, picks the best match, and reconnects if the window restarts.

setup.text: Helps the programmer register the relay with their agent tool, so the agent can find the pairing tools.

protocol.text: The shared message definitions. Each side checks incoming messages against them.

bridge.text: The editor's listener for the relay. It rejects a relay with the wrong secret or version and passes accepted calls to the session. It allows one agent per window.

controller.text: Owns the pairing session: its turn, queue of work, history, and reports. It never touches VS Code directly, so it can be tested with a fake editor.

player.text: Plays queued work at human pace. It also dry-runs each batch first so mistakes surface immediately.

editor.text: The adapter that applies the player's steps to VS Code. It also notices edits the programmer makes and tells the session.

panel.text: A side panel that shows the agent's narration. The programmer uses it to reply, pause, interrupt, or answer a command prompt.

ext.text: Starts the extension and connects the parts. It also saves the session when the window reloads and restores it afterward.

generation.focus: Session Start and Resume — Agent calls start through the MCP relay, which locates the editor window via discovery files, authenticates over WebSocket, reads project guides, and the controller opens a new session or resumes a suspended one after a reload or agent disconnect.

__diagram__.text: Shows what happens when an agent starts pairing: the relay finds the right window, the editor checks the relay, and the session either begins fresh or resumes one left over from a reload.

link.text: Finding the right window and connecting to it.

editor.text: The editor's checks before it accepts the agent.

session.text: Deciding between a new session and a resumed one.

call.text: The agent starts pairing by calling start, optionally with a task and its working folder.

folders.text: The relay lists the folders that might identify the project: the one the agent names, the folders its tool reports, and the relay's own.

guides.text: After the welcome, the relay reads the programmer's rule files (a personal one and project ones) so the agent follows them.

find.text: Each running VS Code window leaves a note saying which folders it has open. The relay prefers the window whose folder most closely contains the project, then the most recently focused one. It ignores windows that have closed.

conn.text: The relay opens a local connection to that window and introduces itself with a secret and a version number.

auth.text: The editor refuses a relay with the wrong secret or version and closes the connection. Otherwise it welcomes the relay.

dispatch.text: The editor allows one agent per window. A second agent's start is refused while the first is active.

susp.text: If a reload or disconnect left a session waiting, the editor checks it before opening a new one.

same.text: A waiting session resumes only when the agent starts from the same folder. A different folder closes the old session.

resume.text: The session picks up where it stopped: same turn, same cursor, same history. The agent is told to re-read files, since it may be a new conversation.

fresh.text: A new, empty session begins with the agent holding the turn.

own.text: The editor remembers which connection owns the session. Only that connection may then send work.

render.text: The relay turns the editor's answer into a report for the agent and appends the pairing guide and the rules it read.

suspend.text: When the window reloads or the agent's connection drops, the session pauses instead of ending. It waits for the agent to start again.

generation.focus: Batch Rehearsal and Playback — A step call's actions are validated and rehearsed in memory, queued (or rejected/discarded), then played by the Player at human pace (move, select, type, delete, point, say, run) and reported back with the resulting code.

nodes.label: Play each action at human pace
Save edited files, capture resulting code
Build report and return to agent

__diagram__.text: Follows one batch of actions from the agent to a report. The editor dry-runs the batch first, so errors return at once rather than minutes into playback.

rehearse.text: The batch runs against a copy of the editor in memory, with no delays and no display. It uses the same player as real playback.

queue.text: The batch joins the queue, remembering the state its dry run produced, so the next batch is checked against it.

play.text: Playing the batch in the editor.

report.text: The controller builds the report, which the relay turns into text for the agent.

recv.text: The agent sends a batch of actions (edit, move, run a command) with its step call.

anchor.text: After a batch stops early, the agent's next batch must say where the cursor is. Without that, the batch is refused, because the agent may be working from a stale picture.

failed.text: If an action would fail, such as text that is not on its line, the whole batch is refused now.

stale.text: If the programmer interrupted during the dry run, the batch was planned without knowing, so it is thrown away.

reject.text: The batch is not queued and nothing changes. The report names the failing action and the reason.

discard.text: The batch is dropped as out of date, and the report says so.

perform.text: Actions play one by one at human pace, including typing rhythm and reading pauses.

interrupted.text: Between actions, the player checks whether the programmer interrupted or an action failed.

finish.text: Edited files are saved, and the resulting code is captured for the report.

stop.text: The batch stops, and queued batches behind it are discarded, since they assumed it would finish.

__diagram__.text: Shows how a terminal command the agent wants to run is saved, approved, executed, and reported. The programmer stays in control: the default is to ask first.

report.text: Telling the agent how it went.

save.text: Edited files are saved first, because the command reads files from disk.

failsave.text: If a save fails, the command does not run and the agent is told why.

need.text: Confirmation is on by default. It is skipped when the setting is off or the programmer already allowed this exact command for the session.

ask.text: The panel shows the command and offers Run, Allow for session, or Skip. Playback waits meanwhile.

decide.text: The programmer's answer decides the next step. An interruption counts as a no.

remember.text: The command joins the session's allowed list, so asking again is unnecessary.

declined.text: The command does not run. The agent is told it was declined, or the batch is interrupted if the programmer interrupted.

exec.text: The command runs in a terminal the programmer can see.

capture.text: The extension collects the end of the output until the command ends or a wait limit passes.

ended.text: The command either finishes within the wait or keeps running.

bg.text: A command still running is reported as running in the background. The panel updates when it exits.

done.text: The report includes the output and exit code. A non-zero exit code marks the action as failed.

__diagram__.text: The states a pairing session moves through, from start to close. Active sessions alternate between agent and programmer turns; reloads and disconnects suspend them rather than end them.

none.text: No session exists in this window.

agentTurn.text: The agent is working: its queued actions play in the editor.

navigator.text: The programmer has taken the turn and edits freely. The agent watches and waits for the hand-back.

suspended.text: The agent is gone, for example after a window reload. The session waits for the agent to start again from the same folder, or for the programmer to end it.

ending.text: The programmer ended the session. The agent receives a final report on its next call.

closed.text: The session is over. Its state clears and the window is ready for a new one.

generation.focus: How AI Pair connects to VS Code and which VS Code components shape its design

rpc.text: VS Code runs extensions in a separate process, so every request has to cross this gap and takes a moment. Everything the extension does crosses this RPC seam, so each editor action is async and can interleave with the programmer typing. Source: src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/common/rpcProtocol.ts (class RPCProtocol). Verified by reading the code.

api.text: This is the one door AI Pair is allowed to use to reach VS Code. The only door in: createApiFactoryAndRegisterActors in src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHost.api.impl.ts:152. Extension targets engines.vscode ^1.106.0; vscode-main is 1.144.0. Verified by reading package.json in both repos.

exttext.text: This is how the agent's cursor and highlights get drawn in the editor. Drives the agent cursor and highlights: createTextEditorDecorationType, setDecorations and revealRange (editor.ts), shown through ExtHostTextEditor in src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTextEditor.ts (setDecorations :532, revealRange :567). onDidChangeTextEditorVisibleRanges / Selection (extHostTextEditors.ts:20-30) are how the programmer scrolling or clicking is noticed as an interruption. Verified by reading the code.

extdoc.text: This is how the agent's edits reach the open files, and how your typing is noticed. Agent edits use workspace.applyEdit (editor.ts, agents.ts), a WorkspaceEdit applied via MainThreadTextEditors / MainThreadDocuments. Programmer typing arrives as onDidChangeTextDocument, which is what makes batches stale. Verified by reading the code.

extterm.text: This is how AI Pair runs a command and learns when it finished. Run commands use createTerminal plus shell integration; the exit code and output come from onDidEndTerminalShellExecution (terminal.ts). Without shell integration there is no end event: src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTerminalShellIntegration.ts:22-39, MainThreadTerminalShellIntegration :17. Verified by reading the code.

extweb.text: This hosts the Pair side panel where the agent's messages appear. The Pair panel is a WebviewView in the secondary sidebar (package.json viewsContainers.secondarySidebar, aiPair.narration). Host side: extHostWebviewView.ts $resolveWebviewView :179. A hidden view is not resolved, so the panel can be absent when the agent calls. Verified by reading the code.

extfs.text: This is how AI Pair notices files changed outside the session. Outside-change tracking uses createFileSystemWatcher and registerFileDecorationProvider (outside_watch.ts): extHostFileSystemEventService.ts:311, extHostDecorations.ts:41. Verified by reading the code.

extcmd.text: This holds the AI Pair commands and the switch that shows or hides them in menus. Commands aiPair.* are registered here; panel.ts sets the aiPair.active context key via the setContext API command (extHostApiCommands.ts:532) that gates menus and the command palette. Verified by reading the code.

extts.text: Start here: this is where VS Code switches AI Pair on and connects its parts. Activates on onStartupFinished (package.json); that event fires after * extensions finish (abstractExtensionService.ts:426). The relay finds this window by workspace folder, not through VS Code. Verified by reading both repos.

__diagram__.text: Design constraints from VS Code that shape AI Pair: (1) a separate extension-host process behind an RPC seam, so edits and cursor moves are async and racy with the programmer; (2) only public vscode API is used, no workbench internals; (3) the panel is a webview in the secondary sidebar and has no access to editors; (4) terminal results depend on shell integration. Verified by reading code in ../vscode-main and packages/vscode.

Why batches are rehearsed and checked for staleness: the programmer and the agent both act on the editor through the same async RPC, so the extension learns of a human edit only after it arrives as an event. Verified by reading the code.
